chunks: 2659 - And Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a woman who wanted to enter iḥrām but feared cracking of the skin; should she dye with henna before that? He said: “I do not like that she do so.”

key_terms.الشُّقَاقَ: cracking or splitting of the skin
key_terms.تُحْرِمَ: to enter the state of iḥrām for hajj or ʿumrah
key_terms.مَا يُعْجِبُنِي: I do not approve or like it

ai.seo_question: Can a woman apply henna before entering iḥrām if she fears her skin will crack?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal question concerning a woman preparing to enter iḥrām and whether she may apply henna beforehand out of fear of skin cracking. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام expresses disapproval of doing so, indicating a ruling of dislike in this context related to the restrictions and etiquette of iḥrām.
